summary: Theorem 1 (computational initialization-faithfulness) overclaims relative to what verify_classical_unrolled_matches_numpy.py actually checks. Paper asserts max_i|x_torch - x_numpy| = 0 under complex64 across 64 seeded frames per N in {512,1024}; verifier asserts relative-L2 < 1e-5 (NOT max-diff zero) under complex128 with 30-frame default. Verifier file exists and is reproducible, but the theorem statement and proof outline must be either (i) weakened to a tolerance-based regression-test claim, or (ii) the verifier strengthened to assert literal bit-exact hard-decision equality at the dtype/frame-count quantifiers in the theorem.

issues.statement: Theorem 1 claims bit-exact equality max_i |x_torch - x_numpy| = 0; verifier asserts worst_x < 1e-5, worst_H < 1e-5, worst_ber < 1e-4 (relative norms, not max-diff zero).
issues.note: Tolerance bounds do not prove exact equality. Counterexample: x_torch = x_np + 1e-8 * x_np passes verifier but max_i|·| != 0. The verifier's PASS condition is strictly weaker than the theorem's claim.

issues.statement: Theorem concerns per-outer-iteration hard-decision QPSK outputs hat{x}_d^{(t)} for every t in {1,...,T_out}; verifier compares only the final out['x_soft'] (continuous) and uses BER difference (aggregate scalar), not per-iteration hard-decision vectors.
issues.note: Two receivers can have identical BER but different decided symbol positions. The 'for every t' quantifier is not verified — no trajectory loop in the verifier.

issues.statement: Paper claims 'fixed verification set of 64 seeded test frames per N in {512, 1024}'. Verifier default is --n-total 512 --frames 30 --snr-list 15 20 25; N=1024 and frames=64 require non-default invocation that the paper does not record.
issues.note: Static configuration mismatch. To recover the theorem's quantifier, the verifier must be re-run with --n-total 1024 and --frames 64 (and the actual run logs committed).

issues.statement: Section 3 surrounding text asserts equivalence under complex64; verifier constructs torch tensors as complex128 / float64 (lines 114-117: torch.complex128, torch.float64; line 171-172: dtype=torch.complex128, rdtype=torch.float64).
issues.note: A double-precision tolerance test does not establish single-precision bit-exactness. Near QPSK decision boundaries, complex64 round-off can flip hard decisions while complex128 does not.

issues.statement: Appendix A claims both NumPy/SciPy and Torch LS solves call the same LAPACK potrs kernel via scipy.linalg.cho_factor and torch.linalg.cholesky_solve; reviewer noted the actual code paths (afdm_baselines.py and classical_joint_unrolled.py) use np.linalg.lstsq/solve and torch.linalg.lstsq/solve, not the asserted Cholesky path.
issues.note: Backend identity (numpy/MKL vs torch CPU/CUDA) is not verified. Different solvers can return different LS solutions under round-off while still passing tolerance.

issues.statement: Appendix asserts same MP-BP Gauss-Seidel sequential update; verifier default is mp_mode='pic' (parallel interference cancellation), not BP. The BP schedule equivalence is asserted, not certified by any verifier run.
issues.note: Vectorized Jacobi-style update vs sequential Gauss-Seidel can diverge while final BER remains similar. Need --mp-mode bp run with per-message comparison to discharge.

issues.statement: Theorem invokes R_torch^{theta=0} with learned-head bias appending zero atoms; verifier default constructs ClassicalJointUnrolled with learnable_heads=() (no heads attached). Optional --with-heads enables heads but it is unclear whether the specific C2-rel support-refinement head described in Section 3.2 is exercised.
issues.note: The default theorem-verification command does not instantiate the learned head that the theorem is about. To support the claim literally, the verifier must instantiate the C2-rel head at zero/no-op bias and re-check equivalence.

issues.statement: Appendix asserts 'The result transfers to any input draw within the same support of the verification distribution ... because the pinning relations are independent of the specific frame realisation.'
issues.note: A finite seeded verifier plus asserted (not formally verified) pinning relations does not imply all simulator draws, especially near argmax ties, prune-threshold flips, or QPSK decision boundaries. The transfer claim is a statistical extrapolation, not a verified consequence.

issues.statement: Appendix asserts deterministic tie-break for OMP argmax and Gray-coded QPSK demap; verifier does not record argmax margins, demap margins, or prune-threshold margins.
issues.note: Equal correlations with tiny backend round-off can select different atoms; equal distances to QPSK symbols can demap differently. To certify the tie-break claim, verifier should log min argmax margin, min demap margin, and min prune margin per frame.

issues.statement: User's invocation describes 'UWA-style 8-path test channel'; verifier defaults to --p-paths 10. Paper Theorem 1 does not explicitly fix P_paths, so this is a configuration-context mismatch rather than a logic gap.
issues.note: Not fatal to Theorem 1 unless the theorem is intended to certify a canonical 8-path setting. Recommend explicit P_paths in either the theorem statement or the committed verifier command.

details.phase_2_skipped_reason: Caller requested verification-only audit; emitting findings without fix-and-recompile loop. User must decide between fix strategies (weaken theorem text vs strengthen verifier) before Phase 2 is appropriate.
